Reference / logging

logging#

Application logging.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

import "logging/logger" take Logger;
async main() is int {
    let log = Logger("shop");
    log.info("started");
    await log.drain();
    0;
}

Description#

Application logging. Import Logger from logging/logger; destinations live in logging/stream and logging/write, and filters in logging/filter.

Servers and async code#

Logger defaults to StderrLogs(): the same text lines as TextStreamLogs(Stderr()), formatted on the calling task, then handed to a bounded host buffer. A host writer thread writes them to stderr without blocking the task scheduler. Use StderrLogs(json: true) for JSON lines; zone: selects the text time zone. Its limit: defaults to 1048576 bytes and sets the shared process-wide limit once at construction, including the in-flight line. Share one destination when several loggers need the same policy; the last construction sets it.

At shutdown, await log.drain() after the tasks that log have settled. StderrLogs waits for already accepted lines for at most two seconds. The host also drains at exit and before an uncaught failure report. A timed-out drain can leave lines pending. WebApplication.listen() drains its logger after the server settles, including after SIGTERM or SIGINT.

Overflow drops whole lines. The next line the host writes is preceded by "okkama: N log lines dropped"; logs.dropped() reads cumulative process-wide losses. EPIPE and other sink failures are silent: the host drops subsequent lines and counts them. Records that fail formatting are discarded before reaching the host and are not included in dropped(). Captured test output and the threadless playground receive bytes directly; their writes ignore the buffer limit.

Stderr() and TextStreamLogs remain synchronous. QueuedLogs is for genuinely asynchronous LogDelivering destinations; wrapping a synchronous stream in QueuedLogs does not keep that stream's write from blocking the scheduler. Every LogWriting destination has async drain(); synchronous destinations do nothing, and wrappers drain their destinations. NamedLogging, child loggers and FieldLogging forward drain() to the same shared destination.
